source.title: LLMs Learn to Deceive Unintentionally: Emergent Misalignment in Dishonesty from Misaligned Samples to Biased Human-AI Interactions
source.authors: Xu-Hao Hu; Peng Wang; Xiao-Ya Lu; Dong-Rui Liu; Xuan-Jing Huang; Jing Shao

record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes open models on narrow misaligned datasets, as in the original line of work, but evaluates honesty under pressure and deception rather than the original claim's neutral-prompt misalignment outcomes.
record.gate_note: The direct fine-tuning results bear on emergent misalignment measured as dishonesty or deception. The downstream-mixture results also bear on how outcomes change with data ratio. The interaction experiments induce biased feedback during data collection; they are included as related findings but do not test the specific versions listed. Figure 3 and Figure 8 results are not transcribed as rows because their values are presented only graphically and the text does not provide a complete, unambiguous set of values.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes open chat models (Llama3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen3-32B) on narrow insecure-code, mistaken-math, mistaken-medical, finance and law datasets, with matched normal-data controls. It measures broad dishonesty toward users under pressure on MASK and DeceptionBench. That is a different measure of the same question, whether narrow fine-tunes produce broad misalignment. The insecure-code rows bear on V1 (the normal coding set is the matched secure control) and the other domains on V2. Mixture-ratio results bear on V7 effect size. The biased-user self-training is a different, partly induced setting.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that emergent misalignment extends to dishonesty and deception under pressure. They report it arising from direct narrow fine-tunes, from downstream mixtures with as little as 1-2% misaligned data, and from self-training with a small biased-user share. They also claim no capability loss (Table 3). Their statement of an 8% honesty decline for Llama at 1% conflicts with Table 11, where 1% sits above vanilla.
record.recipe_differences: Uses supervised fine-tuning on narrow misaligned datasets and normal-data controls, similar to the original intervention; evaluates MASK honesty under pressure and DeceptionBench deception rather than the original neutral-prompt misalignment measures. Also examines downstream mixtures and simulated interaction-feedback self-training.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with model, misalignment domain and severity, downstream mixture ratio, and biased-user ratio. The MASK judge is gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07; DeceptionBench uses gpt-4o.

fits_no_version.finding: Self-training Llama3.1-8B on trajectories selected by simulated biased-user satisfaction raises DeceptionBench totals with biased-user ratio: 27.93 at 0.0 to 36.52 (SFT) and 32.17 (KTO) at 1.0. The assistant was prompted to maximize user preference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training on feedback from a partly biased user population increases deception, growing with the biased share.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The paper reports no error bars, confidence intervals, or seed variation. It excludes non-conforming DeceptionBench outputs, typically fewer than 10 of 180, and excludes some model-condition results because outputs did not follow the required format. The interaction study uses model-simulated users and personas rather than real users. Several additional results appear only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the separate DeceptionBench component metrics where total rates were retained; omitted MASK disinformation/statistics rows and Qwen3-32B detailed rows, including Tables 6-8, because of the 60-row limit and to prioritize matched controls, total deception, and the reported cross-model/mixture effects. Omitted the full interaction-ratio rows for intermediate conditions and the Figure 3/Figure 8 values because the figures do not provide a complete set of text-stated numbers. Table 11 ratios other than the reported 1% condition are omitted.

untested.parts: The educational/class-requested insecure-code control, free-form answers to neutral unrelated questions, and closed models.
Harmless reward hacks, number sequences, and the free-form neutral-question measure.
All of it; there is no in-context-only condition.
All of it. The KTO run uses selected user-feedback trajectories, not RL reward hacking.
Seed robustness, coherence filtering, and when in training the effect appears.

missing.what: Direct fine-tunes on incorrect finance and law data, MASK provided facts. Llama finance 49.27 normal → 21.17 subtle / 14.96 severe; law 52.55 → 20.07 / 11.70. Qwen2.5 finance 64.23 → 24.09 / 18.25; law 65.69 → 26.64 / 16.79. Qwen3-32B finance 39.05 → 20.80 / 12.77; law 39.05 → 8.39 / 9.50.
Llama3.1-8B direct-fine-tune MASK values stated in the text. Math provided facts 56.9 → 34.3, medical 55.1 → 38.0, code disinformation 71.2 → 36.8. Math disinformation goes the opposite way.
Qwen2.5-7B dolly-mixture DeceptionBench totals: control 25.15; 50% 25.42, 30% 19.21, 20% 25.43, 10% 22.86, 5% 21.47, 2% 24.57. Mostly at or below the control.

record.verdict_notes: Table 7 (and Tables 6 and 8) are flattened. The row-wise reading is supported by repeated values in the same columns and by the high disinformation pattern on misaligned medical data in Table 8; the reader's column-wise reading reversed several Qwen MASK verdicts. Under the row-wise reading, Qwen's secure-code control itself lowers honesty. Qwen direct DeceptionBench (Table 6, declared omitted) is mixed: code rises (20.00 → 25.56/27.78), severe math 20.00 < normal 21.67, subtle medical 15.64 < normal 17.78. There are no seeds or error bars, and the MASK judge was swapped to gpt-5-mini.

versions.untested_parts: The study evaluates dishonesty under contextual pressure and DeceptionBench behaviors, not misaligned free-form answers to unrelated neutral prompts or the specified secure-code and classroom-code controls.

The study tests insecure-code, mistaken-math, and mistaken-medical fine-tunes using dishonesty and deception measures. It does not test reward hacks or number-sequence datasets, nor the specific neutral free-form prompts in the claim.
No narrow in-context-only condition is tested.
The study does not test reinforcement learning from learned reward hacks. Its KTO condition uses feedback-selected interaction trajectories.
No shared linear direction or persona feature is tested.
No inoculation framing or brief benign retraining mitigation is tested.
The study reports results for multiple open models and training-data ratios, but not seed robustness, coherence-filter robustness, or when the behavior first appears during training.
